title: Class 2 repetitiveness stems from lack of long-range communication

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Class 2 repetitiveness stems from lack of long-range communication

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Class 2 cellular automata are always eventually repetitive because their lack of long-range communication makes each part behave as an independent system of limited size, typically only a few cells across, and hence with short repetition periods.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the absence of long-range communication effectively forces each part of a class 2 system to behave as if it were a system of limited size.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Systems of Limited Size and Class 2 Behavior” (from p. 255), p. 255. Scope: class 2 cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The behavior and communication range are measurable in existing simulations, and restricted implications may be proved. The universal causal explanation is stronger than finite observations support.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a formal subclass of class 2 rules, measure perturbation cones, domain decomposition, and local temporal periods, then prove or test whether bounded communication implies bounded independent components and eventual periodicity. Counterexamples with persistent long-range dependence would refute the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Global periods can grow despite locally periodic domains.

Class 2 and “part” are informal.

Correlation does not establish the proposed mechanism.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.64
data existence: 0.93

data adequacy: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Once a region is shown to be dynamically finite, eventual repetition is the pigeonhole principle and is settled by proof. Whether rules called class 2 actually break into independent patches a few cells wide is a simulation survey, complete for elementary rules and open beyond them. The causal story is therefore only as strong as the non-circular localization measurement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the spatial range of a one-cell perturbation and the eventual temporal period on class 2 candidates. Given a finite range of a few cells, the pigeonhole bound predicts a short period; a class 2 rule with long-range damage or a nonrepeating evolution would challenge the account.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Localization, short periods, and the class 2 label are easy to make circular.

Typically a few cells needs a survey beyond the usual examples.

The period bound is a theorem only after the finite-range premise is established.
